display.purpose: The site title in the masthead.

display-rail.purpose: The site title in the legend rail at 64rem and more.

headline.purpose: The heading of an area section.

title.purpose: The name link of a repo entry. In the Start here path it is 1.18rem: a link to a page, or plain ink text for a step with links to other sites.

numeral.purpose: The step numbers of the Start here path, muted, in the margin number column.

body.purpose: All running text, in the system sans: 1.03125rem (16.5px at the default 16px), so it follows the default font size of the reader.

body-small.purpose: Entry links, the snapshot line, and the Go deeper line.

label.purpose: Area keys in the legend rail and the hover name of a strip cell. On the capture journey page: the chapter line, the state tags, the stage numbers, and the chapter numbers in the footer. On the roadmap page: the best-guess tag.

label-rail.purpose: The repo names in the upright estate strip, and the station labels of the capture journey track.

label-nav.purpose: The jump links to the areas, and the back links of a text page.

mono.purpose: Commit ids and code only: inline code and code blocks on a text page.

display-text.purpose: The h1 of a text page and of the capture journey page.

headline-text.purpose: The h2 of a text page, under a 2px ink rule, and the h2 of a stage of the capture journey page.

title-text.purpose: The h3 of a text page.

title-small.purpose: The h4 of a text page, with text-wrap: balance.

label-table.purpose: The table heads of a text page and of the At a glance table of the roadmap page, on the surface.

subtitle.purpose: The muted line under the title of the capture journey page.

numeral-station.purpose: The number of a station of the capture journey track, in the ground color on an ink square.

label-bar.purpose: The text of the sticky bar of the capture journey page: "N of M: <stage>" (M is the count of the stages of the chapter), on one line.

label-summary.purpose: The summary of a "For developers" box on the capture journey page.

drawing-title.purpose: The title of a step in a drawing in the site look, and the name of the cloud, of the cylinder, and of a dashed box. Ink, in the drawing font ("Archivo Drawing", weight 600, width 87.5%).

drawing-line.purpose: The other lines of a drawing in the site look, muted, in the drawing font (weight 400, width 87.5%). A repo name is a drawing line too, not monospace. An ink drawing line (the same face and size, in ink) gives a value of a drawn screen or the lead line of a drawing. A date has the form "2 March 2026".

drawing-numeral.purpose: The step number of a drawing in the site look: tabular, in the ground color on a 30-unit ink square, as the station number of the track.

label-snapshot.purpose: The snapshot line of a repo entry on the landing page: the scene date of the map sheet, muted, with tabular figures.

title-fold.purpose: The summary of a fold of the roadmap page: the heading of a section of the source, at the full width.

label-count.purpose: The item count in the summary of a fold of the roadmap page, muted, after a middle dot (“· 3 items”).

shadows.name: ink-edge
shadows.purpose: The 1px ink outline on every area fill (strip cells, mark cells, chips). An outline, not an elevation.

motion.name: ease-cell
motion.purpose: The move of a strip cell color block on hover or focus.

motion.name: duration-cell
motion.purpose: The move of a strip cell color block: 4px up, or 3px right in the legend rail.

motion.name: duration-label
motion.purpose: The fade of the repo name under the strip.

breakpoints.name: phone-title
breakpoints.purpose: The display title takes a width of 78%.

breakpoints.name: strip-links
breakpoints.purpose: A container query on the masthead, computed by build-landing.mjs from the repo counts (CELL_GAP 2px, AREA_GAP 6px): the estate strip (links) replaces the estate mark where each cell can be 24px wide. 422px of strip today (a 462px page at a 16px default font size). It changes with the repo counts.

breakpoints.name: legend-rail
breakpoints.purpose: The sticky 17.5rem legend rail (`--rail`) with the upright estate strip. The rail always shows the links and never the estate mark. The parcel field lies under the rail, with the rail-edge hairline at its edge. `WIDE` in site-html.mjs; `NARROW` (`not all and (min-width: 64rem)`) is its exact opposite and puts the parcel field under the masthead. On a text page the legend rail is sticky, holds the estate mark (up to 13.5rem x .75rem) over the back links, and main is at most 64rem with the reading column at the left.

breakpoints.name: text-page-band
breakpoints.purpose: `NARROW` on a text page, the capture journey page, and a moved page (`mastheadStyle(column)`): the masthead is a band at the top with a hairline below, the estate mark is 8.5rem x .55rem, and the content column is in the center (44rem, or 58rem on the capture journey page).

breakpoints.name: journey-stage-stack
breakpoints.purpose: A container query on `main` of the capture journey page: each stage is one column, and the images come first.

breakpoints.name: journey-track-rows
breakpoints.purpose: A container query on `main` of the capture journey page: a track of up to 4 stations stays in one row, with its line. A longer track is rows of 3 stations with no line (`trackColumns`). A phone screenshot is 130px wide.

breakpoints.name: journey-small-phone
breakpoints.purpose: A container query on `main` of the capture journey page: the image plate of a stage reaches the screen edges (a side padding of .5rem), the stage label column is compact (icon 1.5rem, label .74rem), and the text under the heading takes the full width.

breakpoints.name: journey-track-pairs
breakpoints.purpose: A container query on `main` of the capture journey page: a track of 4 stations is 2 rows of 2, with no line. No station is ever alone in a row (`trackColumns`).

narrative.overview:
The site reads as a land-cover classification map of the code estate. Each area of repos is a land-cover class. Each class has one flat, muted area color. The snapshot commit is the scene date. The reader sees the whole estate in one estate strip, learns the area key, follows the numbered Start here path, and then finds a repo entry with its proof links.

The site look is calm and dense. The page is a mineral ground with evergreen-black ink. Hairline rules divide the content. The parcel field, the faint ink boundaries of made-up field parcels, lies behind the legend rail. It is decoration, not data. Apart from the link blue, the area colors are the only saturated colors on the page, and they fill shapes only. The pages follow the color scheme of the reader, so each color is a pair: one value for light, one value for dark (the `-dark` tokens). The site look refuses the GitHub-clone docs look (the former look) and the stock eco template: no leaf art, no gradients, no drop shadows, no Greenstand logo.

Scope of this record: every page that the site scripts make is in the site look. These pages are the landing page, the text pages, the capture journey pages, the contributors page, the moved pages, and the roadmap page. The shared base is the colors in `.github/scripts/site-colors.mjs` and these parts of `.github/scripts/site-html.mjs`: `siteStyle`, `siteHead`, the estate mark (`estateMark(areas, current)`, `areaGroup`, `areaStyle`), the masthead (`masthead`, `mastheadStyle`), the reading column (`READING_COLUMN`), the content column of the capture journey page (`CONTENT_COLUMN`), the plate edge (`PLATE_EDGE`), the inline code chip (`CODE_CHIP`), the state marks (`STATE_STYLE`), the rules of running text (`TEXT_STYLE`), the area chip (`CHIP_STYLE`), the page footer (`PAGE_END_STYLE`), and the files of the site look (`SITE_LOOK_FILES`: the font and the parcel field). The parcel field is also in the shared base (`.github/scripts/build-parcel-field.mjs` writes `art/parcel-field.svg`). `build-landing.mjs` writes the landing page. `render-md.mjs` writes the text pages: the ecosystem maps, the shared-resource page, the estate glossary, the volunteer guide, and the onboarding guide, the README, and the glossary of each repo. `capture-journey-page.mjs` holds the capture journey page of each chapter, and `build-capture-journey.mjs --site` writes them: `capture-journey.html` for chapter 1 and `capture-journey-<id>.html` for a later chapter (`capture-journey-web-map.html` for chapter 2, `capture-journey-token.html` for chapter 3, and `capture-journey-organizations.html` for chapter 4). `build-moved.mjs` writes the moved pages: a moved page is at the former name of a repo and sends the reader to the new name. `roadmap-page.mjs` holds the roadmap page, and `build-roadmap.mjs --site` writes it (`roadmap.html`). The roadmap page shows the Greenstand roadmap by the areas of the estate. Its text copy for GitHub is `docs/roadmap.md`. Every page shows the parcel field. The former look (`BASE_STYLE`) is not in the build any more.
keyCharacteristics: A mineral ground, an ink text color, and water blue for links only, from one data module of [light, dark] pairs.
Eight area colors (seven land-cover classes and ink for Organization) that fill cells, chips, and rules, never text.
An ink edge on each area fill, so that pale fills stay visible on the ground.
Archivo (a variable face with a width axis) for headings, labels, and numerals; the system sans for body text.
Square corners, hairline rules, and no elevation. Each plate in the surface color has a hairline neatline, as the frame of a map sheet.
The parcel field: the faint, still ink boundaries of made-up field parcels under the legend rail on a wide screen and under the masthead on a phone. The content column stays plain.

The estate strip as the signature: a picture on a phone, a row of links on a wider page, an upright legend in the legend rail on a wide screen. The other pages show it small, as the estate mark in the masthead. On a one-repo page, the locator outlines the cell of that repo.
The capture journey as an ink track: one square station for each stage. A best guess has a hatch, and a part that does not work has a cross.
Diagrams on a plate in the surface color, with each repo node in a tint of its area color.
The roadmap page: one group section for each area in its area color, and each section of the source as a fold with its item count.

rules.name: The One Color, One Job Rule
rules.body: An area color marks its area and nothing else. It fills cells, chips, rules, and tints. It never colors text. Water blue is for links only. The state colors are for states only.

rules.name: The Two Backgrounds Rule
rules.body: Each text color has a contrast of 4.5:1 or more on each background (the ground and the surface), in light and in dark mode. `.github/scripts/check-site-colors.mjs` enforces it in CI. Add a new text color to `TEXTS` in `site-colors.mjs`, so that CI checks it.

rules.name: The State Apart Rule
rules.body: Each area color is 10 or more (CIE76) from each state color, in both schemes. CI enforces it. Thus an area color does not look like a state.

rules.name: The Color-Blind Key Rule
rules.body: Each two area colors are 10 or more apart (CIEDE2000), in both schemes, for normal vision and for simulated protanopia and deuteranopia (Machado 2009, severity 1). CI enforces it. A new area color must pass this check before a page uses it.

rules.name: The Ink Edge Rule
rules.body: Every area fill carries the ink edge (a 1px inset outline in 25% ink). Pale fills, for example Mixed Forest Sage, stay visible on the ground.

rules.name: The Faint Field Rule
rules.body: The parcel field at full mask has a contrast of 1.25:1 or less with the ground, so it stays in the background. Each text color has a contrast of 4.5:1 or more on the field, because the title and the estate strip lie on it. The ink share is above 0 and at most 100. `check-site-colors.mjs` enforces these rules in CI, in light and in dark mode. Today the field is 1.2489:1 (light) and 1.2480:1 (dark) to the ground. The weakest text on the field is best-guess at 4.64:1 and muted at 4.66:1, both in light mode. Change the strength of the field only in `PARCEL_FIELD_INK_SHARE`.

rules.name: The Node Tint Rule
rules.body: The node of a repo in a diagram has a fill of its area color at `DIAGRAM_NODE_TINT` (30%) mixed with the ground. The ink labels have a contrast of 4.5:1 or more on the node tint of each area color, in light and in dark mode. The tint is a percent above 0 and at most 100. `check-site-colors.mjs` enforces these rules in CI. Today the weakest label is ink on the ink tint (Organization): 7.76:1 in light mode and 5.93:1 in dark mode. Change the tint only in `DIAGRAM_NODE_TINT`.

rules.name: The Drawing Colors Rule
rules.body: A drawing in the site look holds the site color block: the 5 neutral colors (ground, surface, ink, muted, line) as CSS custom properties on `svg`, light and dark by `prefers-color-scheme`. An SVG in an `` cannot read the custom properties of the page, so the drawing holds its own copy. `build-capture-journey.mjs` writes the block from `site-colors.mjs` (`DRAWING_COLORS` in `site-drawings.mjs`), and `--site` copies the drawing with the current block. `--check` (CI) fails on a stale block. Each mode fails on a `var(--x)` that is not one of the 5. Each mode also fails on any other color outside the block: a hex color, a color function, a named color, or `currentColor`. A drawing with no site color block fails when it uses `var(--x)` or the drawing font. Thus a drawing in the site look has no area color, no state color, and no link color (the One Color, One Job Rule). A drawing with no site color block keeps its own colors.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Archivo sets headings, labels, and numerals. The system sans sets the body text. Monospace sets code and commit ids only.

rules.name: The Narrow Label Rule
rules.body: Archivo labels use a width of 87.5%. Numerals use a width of 75%. The full width is for headings. Headings use `text-wrap: balance`.

rules.name: The No Lone Word Rule
rules.body: `siteStyle` sets `text-wrap: pretty` on paragraphs, list items, `dd`, and quotes, on every page in the site look. Thus the browser avoids one word alone on the last line of a paragraph.

rules.name: The Whole Name Rule
rules.body: A date (YYYY-MM-DD), a repo name, a quoted group in parentheses (for example "(Complete)"), and the last word of a fold heading with its count and its tag stay on one line, in a nowrap span. A browser breaks a line at a hyphen and between an opening quote and "(", and a count must not stand alone on a line. The roadmap page puts the spans in the text between the tags.

rules.name: The Drawing Font Rule
rules.body: All text of a drawing in the site look is in the drawing font. The system sans is only its fallback. When the words of a drawing change, run `subset-drawing-font.py`, so that the drawing font has each character.

rules.name: The 24 px Target Rule
rules.body: A strip cell is a link only where it can be 24px wide. Below that width, the strip is the estate mark: a picture with no links and no words, hidden from screen readers. Do not hard-code the width; compute it from the repo counts and test it on the masthead container, not on the page. In the legend rail each row is at least `max(1.5rem, 24px)` high, so the rail always has links.

rules.name: The Flat Map Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at all times. Use tone (the surface), the neatline, and hairlines for structure. Use no drop shadow and no gradient. The one exception is the scroll shadows of a wide diagram: they are the cue that a diagram scrolls, and they show nowhere else. The parcel field is a flat ink layer behind the page, not a surface above it.

rules.name: The Neatline Rule
rules.body: Each plate in the surface color carries `PLATE_EDGE` (1px solid, the line color). Take the edge from `PLATE_EDGE`; do not write a new border value for a plate.

rules.name: The One Frame Rule
rules.body: A plate that holds framed images has no neatline: a frame inside a frame is noise. The image plate of a capture journey stage has no edge, because each phone screenshot has its ink edge outline and each drawing has its hairline border.

rules.name: The Locator Rule
rules.body: The estate mark outlines one cell at most: the cell of the repo of a one-repo page. The outline is ink (2px solid, 1px offset), never an area color. A page about more than one repo shows no locator.

dos: Do take every color from `BACKGROUNDS`, `TEXTS`, `STATES`, `LINES`, and `AREA_COLORS` in `site-colors.mjs`, as a [light, dark] pair, through the CSS custom properties of `siteStyle`.

Do define every custom property that a page uses. `build-landing.mjs`, `render-md.mjs`, `build-capture-journey.mjs`, `build-moved.mjs`, `build-contributors.mjs`, and `build-roadmap.mjs --site` fail when a page uses a custom property that nothing defines (`undefinedProperties` in `site-html.mjs`; the check skips scripts).

Do let a page build fail when a file that the page loads is missing. `build-landing.mjs`, `render-md.mjs`, `build-capture-journey.mjs --site`, `build-moved.mjs`, and `build-roadmap.mjs --site` check the files of the site look (`SITE_LOOK_FILES`: the font and the parcel field) and show every missing file at once. `render-md.mjs` also checks Mermaid for a page with a diagram. The contributors page is built in a job with no site (`build-contributors.mjs --out`), so `build-landing.mjs` checks its files: it fails when the page, the font, or the parcel field is missing from the site.
